findings.claim: The closing sequence distinguishes return as the transfer into divine custody from the counting and review that follow it as account placed upon Us.

findings.reader_payoff: Return and reckoning become two connected movements: arrival places the group before the authority, and account examines what has arrived.
findings.containment: This is an attributed, strong HFT synthesis with exact three-ayah anchors, legacy-unbound identity, and absent target morphology. It distinguishes the supplied sequence without forcing a complete legal chronology or replacing the plain return reading.

epistemic.reason: The HFT trace explicitly supplies punishment, divine agency, return, counting, review, and the connective sequence, but the source is legacy-unbound and target morphology is surface-only.

findings.title: Setting and assigned return
findings.claim: By analogy with the sun's setting between sky and earth, the focus's return can be pictured as a course reaching its assigned place rather than simple disappearance from the present field.
findings.mechanism: The supplied focus branch carries the sun's movement to its setting-place, while the sky and earth anchors provide the upper and lower visual field; that contact gives human disappearance a bounded temporal-spatial image without changing the human reference of هُمْ.
findings.reader_payoff: The return clause can hold an image of vanishing from sight as arrival at a place, so absence is perceived as the closure of a course as well as the plain fact of return.
findings.containment: This is an exploratory, attributed analogy. The packet explicitly warns that هُمْ denotes persons, not the sun; the solar-setting image is therefore a bounded comparison and never a lexical replacement for human إِيَاب.

epistemic.reason: The HFT outlier supplies exact sky, earth, and focus anchors and an explicit containment statement, but it is exploratory, legacy-unbound, and target morphology is absent.
